rule: Every required column is present, and check_number, date, routing_number, account_last4, micr_line and status are filled on every row.
why_it_matters: A row without its check number or account can't be matched to the bank statement.

rule: amount is positive with two decimals, digits only (no $ or commas). Blank only on a void check.
why_it_matters: Figures with symbols sort and sum as text in a spreadsheet.

rule: The written amount can be read as a number.
why_it_matters: If the words can't be read, the legal amount is unknown and the check needs a human.

rule: The written amount and the amount in figures agree to the cent.
why_it_matters: Under UCC 3-114, words prevail over numbers when they conflict. A mismatch is either a misread or a check written wrong; both need a look before the row is trusted.

rule: The routing number passes the ABA checksum: 3(d1+d4+d7) + 7(d2+d5+d8) + (d3+d6+d9) is a multiple of 10.
why_it_matters: One misread MICR digit almost always breaks the checksum.

rule: The first two digits of the routing number are in an assigned Federal Reserve range (00-12 or 21-32; 61-72 and 80 for special use).
why_it_matters: The fictional samples use 5x prefixes on purpose so they never match a real bank; real checks should not.

rule: The check number in the MICR line matches the printed check number.
why_it_matters: A mismatch means one of them was read wrong or the check was printed on someone else's stock.

rule: The routing number field matches the routing number in the MICR line.
why_it_matters: The field should come from the MICR line and agree with it.

rule: The account number in the MICR line ends with account_last4.
why_it_matters: Keeps checks from two accounts out of one register.

rule: No check number appears twice in one account.
why_it_matters: A duplicate is a scan read twice or a reused check number; either way the books would double count it.

rule: Check numbers run in sequence, or the missing number is in the register as void or stopped.
why_it_matters: Gaps are where missing checks hide. Auditors ask about every one.

rule: date and cleared_date are real calendar dates and a check does not clear before the date written on it.
why_it_matters: A check that cleared before it was written means a misread date.

rule: A void check has status void, no amount and 'VOID' as the written amount.
why_it_matters: Keeps a voided check in the sequence without adding to any total.

rule: Cleared checks with a cleared_date in the statement period add up to the statement's printed checks-paid total and count.
why_it_matters: The register and the bank agree on what cleared. This is the check that catches a missed scan.

rule: payee is filled on every check that is not void.
why_it_matters: A check without a payee can't be categorized.

rule: status is cleared only when cleared_date is filled.
why_it_matters: An outstanding check marked cleared hides an open item at reconciliation.
